notes.title: BATTLEZONE®: COMBAT COMMANDER LAUNCHES MARCH 1ST 2018
notes.content:
BATTLEZONE®: COMBAT COMMANDER brings its inimitable fusion of shooter and strategy action to PC in a month's time. The remaster of Battlezone® 2 will launch on Steam on March 1st 2018!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bro9xSKKWKA&feature=youtu.be
Today's "Graphics Comparison" trailer showcases the impressive visual enhancements coming to BATTLEZONE®: COMBAT COMMANDER, including updated art and effects, DirectX 11 rendering and shading, 4K resolution support, and retextured and upscaled terrain. Big Boat Interactive’s remaster will also offer cross-play online multiplayer across Steam and GOG, support for both online and LAN multiplayer, achievements, cloud saves*, support for the game’s two-decade old modding scene, and many other refinements and tweaks. 

February Beta
The independent developer and publisher also confirmed that a beta is planned for the community in February. Players can sign up for more information here: www.rebellion.com/bzcc 
 
Website and info
For more on the game’s features, screenshots, video and more head to www.BattlezoneCC.com

notes.title: Battlezone: Combat Commander - Coming soon to Steam!
notes.content:
BATTLEZONE® COMBAT COMMANDER REMASTERS THE CLASSIC FPS-RTS

https://i.imgur.com/BB374kf.jpg

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QB9eqiT_a7c&feature=youtu.be
Independent UK developer and publisher Rebellion® is delighted to reveal BATTLEZONE® COMBAT COMMANDER, deploying to PC in 2018.

https://i.imgur.com/PydNAYq.jpg
 
After Rebellion®'s TIGA Award-nominated remaster of Battlezone® (1998), many fans of the pioneering FPS-RTS hybrid asked for its acclaimed sequel, Battlezone® II: Combat Commander, to receive the same treatment. 
 
Developed by Big Boat Interactive and published by Rebellion®, BATTLEZONE® COMBAT COMMANDER remasters Battlezone® II with slick new visuals, mod support for the game's two-decade old modding scene, cross-play online multiplayer between GOG & Steam for up to 14 players, achievements, cloud saves* and more.
 
A mysterious alien force threatens humanity itself. In this galaxy-wide war, you are in command of the resistance. Leading from the front, you take to the battlefield in thrilling first-person combat, piloting futuristic, customizable war machines including hover-tanks, colossal mech walkers, lightning-fast mortar-bikes and more.

https://i.imgur.com/nNxBruJ.jpg
 
But you don't just fight from the front - you are in total command! A gripping singleplayer campaign will test your mettle as you learn to plot strategy, construct bases, form your armies, deploy defenses and call in airstrikes. Achieving victory is no mean feat in this remarkable blend of classic real-time strategy and first-person action. To save humanity, you must prove yourself a true combat commander! 
 
BATTLEZONE® COMBAT COMMANDER is coming to Steam in 2018.
 
Ahead of launch, fans can sign up for a chance to be a part of the game's closed beta at rebellion.com/bzcc 

https://i.imgur.com/kAEwuSr.jpg
 
About Rebellion®
Founded in 1992, Rebellion® is one of Europe's leading independent game developers and publishers. Whether it's the breathtaking intensity of Sniper Elite 4, the face-hugging terror of Aliens vs. Predator or the grindhouse frenzy of Zombie Army Trilogy, the Oxford-based studio is known for creating stand-out games that thrill players. www.rebellion.com 
 
About Big Boat Interactive
Big Boat Interactive is an independent development studio based out of Los Angeles and run by game industry veteran Mike Arkin. Big Boat specializes in toy-connected mobile apps and remasters of classic games.

notes.title: BATTLEZONE® 98 REDUX COMING TO MAC & IPAD
notes.content:
http://i.imgur.com/wTDTRdp.jpg

We have an exciting announcement for Battlezone 98 fans on Apple devices - Battlezone 98 Redux will launch on Mac (Steam and Mac App Store) and iPad (iOS 10 devices and above) this Spring!

Players buying through the Mac and iOS App Stores will be able to to purchase the Battlezone 98 Redux Odyssey Edition including both the base game and its massive expansion "The Red Odyssey" in one great value package!

Mac players on Steam will be able to buy the base game and expansion separately.

Battlezone 98 Redux Odyssey Edition includes:
Four explosive singleplayer campaigns across 52 missions and 9 planetary environments   
Competitive cross-platform multiplayer between Mac and PC for 2-8 players
Re-modelled, high-polygon vehicles, buildings and terrain
Upgraded lighting, shadows, and improved particle effects
Access to a wealth of community-created mod content via Steam Workshop, ModDB.com and the game's powerful map editor.

NEW PATCH INCOMING!
News of the Mac and iPad versions comes as a substantial new patch for BATTLEZONE® 98 REDUX prepares for deployment on PC. Launching next week, the update delivers impressive visual upgrades including improved shadowing and shader effects, extended mod compatibility across multiplayer, the ability to create custom campaigns and numerous tweaks and fixes.


http://i.imgur.com/sxSG0Dp.jpg

notes.title: Patch Notes - The Red Odyssey 24/08/2016!
notes.content:
Mission Tuning
CH02 Mission - Stop bug that could cause unlimited spawning of hunters and reduce enemies in the waves to make less difficult at medium and higher difficulties.
CH03 Mission - Fixed howitzers to work as intended and fixed mine field to be effective against player
CH04 Mission - Add an abandoned enemy ship to make the retreat after discovery possible.
CH08 Mission - Adds time to end so final VO completes
CH09 Mission - Reduce difficulty.  The longer cover is maintained, the fewer enemies spawned when cover is finally left.  Enemies turrets also became single weapon turrets
BD02 Mission - Reduced difficulty.
BD03 Mission - Difficulty tuned, and several object spawning on top of each other issues fixed.
BD04 Mission - Startup issues fixed.  Scavenger's shouldn't leave early which made it hard for new players to follow them. Final chase made more survivable while leaving the epic chase feeling intact.
BD06 Mission - Enemy attack waves slightly reduced
General
A number of minor model fixes applied
Fixed error with point lights.  Weapon fire shouldn't cause strange reverse shadows anymore.
Chinese Scavenger emissive fixed (strange glow removed)
TRO Music Added to game, and TRO missions play TRO sound files
Fury hybrids no longer describe themselves as scavengers
Black Dog weapon properly rotates only top to shoot now.
CVHAUL adjusted how it holds items so it can't levitate itself
Fixes BD constructor's description text.
Non-playing sounds for several vehicles such as CH Constructor fixed.
Fixed the CVAPC cockpit

The Patch also includes
Mod samples in Edit Mode fixed to be present and useful samples

notes.title: Battlezone 98 Mod Competition Winners
notes.content:
Firstly we’d like to say a big thank you to everyone that entered the competition, it’s been awesome to see new mods appearing on the store that have had such thought, time, and effort put in to them. We know the Battlezone 98 Redux community is a fantastic community, but the level of some of the mods that we saw was beyond anything we could have thought! As a thank you to everyone who entered a mod, we’re pleased to announce that you will all receive a Rebellion game of your choice! (Instructions of how to claim your game are at the bottom of this post)

Secondly, we’d like to thank AMD Gaming for sponsoring this competition by generously providing us with a number of CPUs!

Lastly, we want to say congratulations to our top 10 modders! It was a difficult process to whittle down the entrants in to a top 10 as the standard of mods was extremely high, but below you can see who won and where you can find their mod! It’s hugely inspiring to see what you guys created and we hope inspires others to give it a go. In our eyes, everyone is a winner as they get to play the mods! So without further ado, we present the top 10!

10.  The Space Race Aint Over! - Headcrab AddictLINK
A personal favourite of some members here at Rebellion, this mod allows the player to race against three other AI controlled vehicles in a map that feels very similar to the pod race on Tatooine! The developer has said that multiplayer is planned, and once this is available it will be a definite mod to try.http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/264969860601444653/E046DDB0C828FF5F3CCCA3237631AB2C92B2D414/

9. American Pilot - CuddlyKittenLINK
Created as a result of the American faction not having an awesome looking outfit and the Chinese having a devious Red outfit, this mod gives your pilot a fresh space suit, complete with stars and stripes. Both the reasoning behind this and the design give this mod a definite space in our top 10!http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/275102315866471473/E7E48BF829356BF5E6AE4D2F2575674A7EC4109E/

8. More Realistic American Vehicles – Owenc3LINK
Continuing with the American theme, this mod overhauls all the American vehicles, giving them a fresh new lick of paint, including the token flag on the side. This mod also sees buildings being given a fresh new look, with awesome panels (possibly solar?) and gold touches. Bonus points also given for the overhaul to the Moonlander! http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/1613797962857472414/1DD54FF4CF1D292C4996E95607ACA17F7A20B52C/

7. Black Dog Elite Pilots - MazizLINK
We love a good pilot mod. This mod gives your soldier a Black Dog makeover, adding a black suit, and new goggles. Complete with a black dog patch, this mod will make you feel like a real pro when you play, and strike fear in to the heart of your enemies!http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/264969860598854936/2D113591419EA38E5A0C60E8B2DC6F0266EAC913/

6. Weapon Prototypes – FrenchoxLINK
With over 15 prototype weapons this mod is a shed load of fun, including mortars that almost level an entire playing field, a state of the art Virus Vploader weapon (not a real virus!) and neon lazers! This mod was a personal favourite of a few players here and we look forward to seeing more of it!http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/269472527195862480/9F8E89F31DB89D1E454DA1375F1BD107D0707BA8/

5. Sphelx Komodo Wireframe Set – Sphelx KomodoLINK
Harking back to the original Battlezone game, this funky mod turns the map into a green and black grid, as well as gives you a neon green tank and bomber to fly around in! For pure originality and the nostalgia trip, this gets a place in the top 5! We’re very much hoping for more of this...http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/261591516979946108/317CE34C9C16495E4BB4A077ABEC534EFDC550CD/

4. Japanese Rocket Tank – SystemeLINK
Systeme did something we weren’t sure possible, created a new vehicle type. With an edited back section this new ship is a play on the American Rocket Tank, but with a Japanese makeover and a stylish new rear section. This has garnered a lot of attention in the forums, and we’re keen to see how he accomplished this feat. Hopefully this will start a new wave of vehicle mods! We’ll have t wait and see...http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/261591516983561017/F6EA5C4C10BB717CAD291CC67576E8A9A418845D/

3. Advanced Combat Training – GeneralBlackDragonLINK
With a mod that has even taught some of the old dogs new tricks, the Advanced Combat Training mod has gained some serious praise from veteran modders, with some calling for it to be included as a stock training mission! One modder said “this mission is a very well made script designed to help new players get acquainted with vehicular combat. The constant VOs feel interactive and the mission even helped me (a player of over 8 years) get better at dodging rounds! Overall a very nice and educational experience”. Some serious praise indeed, well done to you!http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/263843003890300206/B37A8DD4BED716FB2F8FEC452A6870879035CA7C/

2. Chicken Farm – The Deus ExLINK
Many a man-hour was lost to Chicken Farm here at Rebellion. This light hearted multiplayer map adds a new game type in which each player must collect as many chickens as possible, while trying to distract other players. Perfect for casual gamers, this mod is a lot of fun, and even includes chicken themed weaponry (complete with homemade chicken noises!). We’d recommend you play with more than 3 players as the most fun is when you’re all running around each other. Download this, it’s truly eggs-celent...http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/268347610994642457/9E261B0766FAF8AADA841DC293D0020610CF31F0/

1.  Burns Rebellion – CONGRATULATIONS ScrapPoolLINK
We could describe this, or we could let one of our veteran modders do it... 

“This is without doubt the largest and most ambitious entry, and it covers  just about every discipline imaginable; there are new textures, new maps, new mission scripts, new weapons, new units, new story, and future versions come with the promise of completely new voiceovers.

I've always been a sucker for well-crafted narrative content, and this example is particularly welcome given that it patches perhaps the most hotly debated hole in the Battlezone timeline; Project Pedigree. 

Consider Burns' Rebellion the missing link between Battlezone and Battlezone II; it's worthy of it. The sheer quality in these two missions - and there's a third planned - is well above even that of the original game. 

ScrapPool has once again demonstrated his mastery of a great many disciplines.”

That’s some serious praise, and this mod duly deserves it. A lot of time and effort has been put in to this, and for that, it deserves top prize of the gaming laptop!http://images.akamai.steamusercontent.com/ugc/263843960694752154/FF3A5BEA5E3D75BC322901D5F4F22FE4228812A1/

So there we go, there’s your top 10! We highly recommend you head over to Steam to try them out and let the modders know what you think. Once again, a huge thank you and congratulations to everyone who entered, you’re the best!

HOW TO CLAIM A PRIZE
Simply add the rebellionbattlezone account as a friend on the account you won a prize with. Will then contact you over the next few days with sorting out your prize.

notes.title: BATTLEZONE 98 REDUX DEV BLOG 2
notes.content:
http://www.rebellion.co.uk/media/W1siZiIsIjIwMTYvMDQvMTUvMTVfMTRfNTZfMjMxX1RhbmtUZXguanBnIl0sWyJwIiwidGh1bWIiLCI2NDd4MzMzIyJdXQ/TankTex.jpg

Battlezone 98 fans... it's nearly here! 

As we get closer and closer to the launch of Battlezone 98 Redux ,we're excited to continue our dev blog series as we delve deep into the remaster's development. Here, courtesy of producer Mike Arkin, is the second entry in the series, in which Mike talks about how his team have given Redux's models a thorough makeover. 

Hi, my name is Mike Arkin and I’m the producer of Battlezone 98 Redux. By strange coincidence, I was also a member of the original team that launched Battlezone in 1998. In this second dev diary I’m going to talk about what we did to enhance the art for Redux - specifically the vehicle and building models.

In 1998, the state-of-the-art in 3D games was very different to what it is today. Back then, the Grizzly tank was made up of about 300 polygons and it had a single texture that was 128 pixels by 128 pixels i.e. an 8-bit image! We thought it looked great at the time, but bear in mind that the average PC didn’t even have a 3D card back then and when they did, our target was a card with 4MB of ram. 4 megabytes! Yikes.

A GRIZZLY TRANSFORMATION

Here is what that Grizzly looked like. Notice how rough the textures are and how, because the models have such low polygon counts, there is almost no detail - it’s all just flat.

http://i.imgur.com/ltze484.jpg
http://i.imgur.com/n7PIFEF.jpg

Fast forward 17 years later and PCs are a just a little bit faster. And we really wanted to make Battlezone 98 Redux shine. So the first step was to remodel all the tanks at a much more reasonable level of detail, at around 8000-10,000 polygons in fact.  We actually used the original models as reference since it was important to us that the vehicles in game felt familiar. We wanted the same shape, but better looking.

We didn’t actually have the original models from scratch, but using a utility called NOESIS we were able to convert the cooked game assets back into a format called FBX. This meant we could use the exact models and textures as a basis for the new models.

So, here is the new Grizzly model. Notice we added lots of detail and rounded all the sharp edges a bit.  The tank barrel is no longer just a long rectangle as we gave it some flutes and an actual opening.

http://i.imgur.com/Mb7Ue8G.jpg

LET'S GET READY TO RUMBLE!

Once we did that, it was time for new textures.  With our minimum specifications just a bit upgraded from the 4MB days, we were able to redo the textures to match the new models.

The end result:  2048x2048 per vehicle with even larger textures for larger buildings

Here is the texture for the new Grizzly…

http://i.imgur.com/gpJHjnG.jpg

And here is the textured Grizzly …looking good, baby, ready for outer space war!

http://i.imgur.com/GflcyWL.jpg

We really wanted to keep the look of the original tank through key elements like the star and eye decor.  We also wanted to retain the roughened, rugged look from the original game, which was very different then the super clean look of Battlezone 2.

But wait, there’s more! Video cards now have programmable shaders, and modern shaders can read multiple textures, so we didn’t just use a single texture like we did in the original game.

We added a few extra bits like a specular map to show where the vehicle should be shiny.

http://i.imgur.com/u9W4see.jpg

And a normal map, which helps to show the way light reflects.

http://i.imgur.com/YzQYiSu.jpg

And an emissive map, which shows where on the vehicle there is light being emitted.

http://i.imgur.com/S1EumE5.jpg

The emissive map is great because now we can have things glow, and we’ve sure made a bunch of things glow. Once we saw it in action we wanted things to really pop, so we added a full screen shader to make all the emissive effects on screen have a super glow effect. 

Which, I think you’ll agree, looks superb.

THE FINAL RESULT

So when you put it all together, you can see that our tanks (and buildings) look fantastic!

http://i.imgur.com/fmqv5vr.jpg

One of the other things we could do with these fancy new shaders was real-time shadowing, so now as you can see the tank has some nice fancy lighting which now includes-self shadowing.  If you don’t know the term, self shadowing means the light from the sun causes parts of the vehicles to cast shadows onto themselves.  So, for example, the tank gun casts a shadow onto the tank.

Even the old boxy pilot got a makeover!

http://i.imgur.com/aKSX2Hx.jpg

He’s not just blessed with a high polygon count and a fancy new texture. Now he’s a skinned model with 18 animations.  That’s about 15 more than the original!

So there you go, high-poly models, fantastic textures and modern shaders, took us from here...

http://i.imgur.com/n7PIFEF.jpg

To here:

http://i.imgur.com/GflcyWL.jpg

Not bad, right?

Thanks again for reading! We can’t wait to show you Battlezone 98 Redux very soon. As ever, if you have any questions or want more info, feel free on the Steam forums – I’d love to respond to you!

Look out for more posts in the coming days, and make sure to stay tuned to Battlezone 98 Redux's Steam page and our Twitter and Facebook feeds for the latest news. 

Battlezone 98 Redux is coming to Steam this spring.

LET'S GET READY TO RUMBLE!

Once we did that, it was time for new textures.  With our minimum specifications just a bit upgraded from the 4MB days, we were able to redo the textures to match the new models.

The end result:  2048x2048 per vehicle with even larger textures for larger buildings

Here is the texture for the new Grizzly…

http://i.imgur.com/gpJHjnG.jpg

And here is the textured Grizzly …looking good, baby, ready for outer space war!

http://i.imgur.com/GflcyWL.jpg

We really wanted to keep the look of the original tank through key elements like the star and eye decor.  We also wanted to retain the roughened, rugged look from the original game, which was very different then the super clean look of Battlezone 2.

But wait, there’s more! Video cards now have programmable shaders, and modern shaders can read multiple textures, so we didn’t just use a single texture like we did in the original game.

We added a few extra bits like a specular map to show where the vehicle should be shiny.

http://i.imgur.com/u9W4see.jpg

And a normal map, which helps to show the way light reflects.

http://i.imgur.com/YzQYiSu.jpg

And an emissive map, which shows where on the vehicle there is light being emitted.

http://i.imgur.com/S1EumE5.jpg

The emissive map is great because now we can have things glow, and we’ve sure made a bunch of things glow. Once we saw it in action we wanted things to really pop, so we added a full screen shader to make all the emissive effects on screen have a super glow effect. 

Which, I think you’ll agree, looks superb.

THE FINAL RESULT

So when you put it all together, you can see that our tanks (and buildings) look fantastic!

http://i.imgur.com/fmqv5vr.jpg

One of the other things we could do with these fancy new shaders was real-time shadowing, so now as you can see the tank has some nice fancy lighting which now includes-self shadowing.  If you don’t know the term, self shadowing means the light from the sun causes parts of the vehicles to cast shadows onto themselves.  So, for example, the tank gun casts a shadow onto the tank.

Even the old boxy pilot got a makeover!

http://i.imgur.com/aKSX2Hx.jpg

He’s not just blessed with a high polygon count and a fancy new texture. Now he’s a skinned model with 18 animations.  That’s about 15 more than the original!

So there you go, high-poly models, fantastic textures and modern shaders, took us from here...

http://i.imgur.com/n7PIFEF.jpg

To here:

http://i.imgur.com/GflcyWL.jpg

Not bad, right?

notes.title: BATTLEZONE 98 REDUX DEV BLOG 1
notes.content:
http://www.rebellion.co.uk/media/W1siZiIsIjIwMTYvMDQvMDcvMTZfMTFfNTVfNTAyX29uZS5qcGciXSxbInAiLCJ0aHVtYiIsIjY0N3gzMzMjIl1d/one.jpg

Battlezone 98 fans... it's nearly here! 

As we get closer and closer to the launch of Battlezone 98 Redux ,we're excited to share with you a brand new dev blog series that will delve deep into the remaster's development. Here, courtesy of producer Mike Arkin, is the very first post. Further posts will go into even more detail, but to kick us off, here's a guide for what to expect from Battlezone 98 Redux!

Hi, my name is Mike Arkin and I’m the producer of Battlezone 98: Redux. By strange coincidence, I was also a member of the original team that launched Battlezone in 1998.

Since announcing Battlezone 98 Redux I’ve often been asked what a remaster means. While there is no one definition of a game remaster, I thought I’d use this first dev diary to explain what this remaster is.

Our high concept when we planned this project was to preserve the original gameplay, but enhance and augment the game in every way we could.  Keep in mind that we constantly struggle with the idea that we want to make the game as modern as possible, but we also need to service the fans that have been playing Battlezone for so many years and have kept the community alive. It’s hard to please everyone, but I’m pretty sure that most people will be happy with what we’ve done.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bp57Lo2grfM

OUT WITH THE OLD, IN WITH THE NEW...
So what did we do? Well, the short version is that we’re still working with the old engine, but we have ripped pieces out and replaced them with modern features.  Also, we’ve replaced most if not all of the art in the game with modern versions.  Some of the art looks similar to the original since we used all of the old art as reference, but when you put the two side by side the difference is clear.

We’ve not redesigned the game, though. Instead, we’ve strived to make the game we would have made in 1998 if PCs were 100 times more powerful back then, like they are now. In fact, based on some quick math, maybe perhaps 1000 is a better number (our minimum spec back in 1998 was a Pentium 90!).

LET THERE BE LIGHT...
The longer version?  For starters, we introduced a shader-based DirectX 9 renderer which allowed us to use an all new shader/material system throughout the game. All vehicles and buildings were remodeled and retextured in high resolution and high polygon meshes. We also used advanced shader techniques to add a little glow and shine to the new models.

And what’s the point of shine if we don’t have lights? So of course we added headlights to all the tanks and adapted the system to allow for real-time lighting.

Speaking of lighting, we now have a real lighting system, and all game objects like vehicles and buildings cast shadows and self-shadow! You might be thinking that Battlezone had shadows in 1998, but really it just had blobs, not actual projected shadows with soft edges like Battlezone 98 Redux has.

HEADS UP!
The in-game heads-up display (HUD) was also completely redesigned. And we’ve made it scalable so at higher resolutions it looks nice and sharp. This also means that if you have a giant monitor you can now have your HUD scale up way high, or dial it back down if you’d prefer! Oh, and the Russian vehicles now have their own HUD, as do the mysterious Furies!

http://i.imgur.com/1ylyEW5.jpg

Here is the stock HUD at 4x resolution (click for the full image)

EARTHSHATTERING ...
One of the most interesting changes we made (and the subject of one of my next blogs) is the terrain.  Since Battlezone 98 Redux takes place in space on various barren planets, the terrain is really important since for many levels it’s most of what’s on screen.  Also, it makes up a very large percentage of a user generated level, so it was vital to make the new terrain compatible with old maps.  

So we rewrote the terrain system, cranked up the mesh to four times the current resolution, did a little shader magic to eliminate seams, added specular and normal maps to keep things interesting, and we added a detail texture to all the terrain tiles.  The end result is terrain that is the same size and shape of the original terrain, but so much better looking. 

http://i.imgur.com/nEqAkYG.jpg

Check out that terrain! (click for full image) 

BACK TO THE FUTURE
And, since we retained compatibility with all of the old file formats, all the user generated maps created over the years can go through a five-minute conversion process and run in Battlezone 98 Redux with upgraded assets. When an old map is loaded Battlezone 98 Redux takes care of upscaling and smoothing automatically, so it’s easy and quick to convert and modernize any map.  

Speaking of which, back in 1998 we shipped the game with the tools we used to make the game. Crude tools, sure, but they were good enough that a healthy map and mod community grew over 17 years! 

Well, Battlezone 98: Redux goes one step further by adding Steam Workshop support and a host of in-game options for pulling your new content into the game and running it.  No longer do you need to edit text files to add a MP map; now the map is recognized and will be displayed in-game, ready to play!  No longer do you need to load Instant Action missions from the command line; now all of your IA missions are displayed in a menu ready to load with a few mouse clicks! And for game mods, there is now a Mod menu where you can activate and deactivate mods simply and easily.

http://i.imgur.com/8SwfGcK.jpg

Here is the Mod selection screen with four mods loaded and active (click for full image) 

In fact, there’s a dedicated group of map makers that have already converted maps and loaded them onto Steam Workshop so they are ready to go! So yes, when we launch Battlezone 98 Redux there will be plenty of content available on Steam Workshop, day 1.

These are the highlights of what’s new in Battlezone 98 Redux, but there are a host of other changes and improvements to the game which I’ll cover in future blog posts. Things like multiplayer, bug and AI fixes, menus and fonts. I’ll also get into some of the more detailed specifics of the vehicles, terrains and so on. Until then, thanks for reading and for your continued support of Battlezone 98 Redux. We can’t wait to finally show you the finished game very soon. If you have questions or want more info, feel free to post on the Steam forums – I’d love to respond to you!

Look out for more posts in the coming days, and make sure to stay tuned to the Battlezone 98 Redux's Steam page and our Twitter and Facebook feeds for the latest news. Battlezone 98 Redux is coming to Steam this spring...

notes.title: BATTLEZONE 98 REDUX LAUNCHES SPRING 2016
notes.content:
http://i.imgur.com/8nqZrt9.png?1
Rebellion are delighted to reveal much anticipated remaster of Battlezone (1998) - one of the greatest sci-fi strategy titles ever made (in our opinion)!

 Watch the Battlezone 98 Redux reveal trailer 

Launching on Steam for PC this Spring, Battlezone 98 Redux keeps the core rush of first-person action and RTS gameplay that earned widespread critical acclaim, and blends it with remastered visuals, online multiplayer and the potential for near limitless new content with support for Steam Workshop mods!

Made by devs from the original Battlezone (1998)
As lots of you reading this will know, Battlezone (1998)’s revolutionary gameplay fostered a really strong community that still develops mods for the game to this day.

To ensure Battlezone 98 Redux remained faithful to the community, we enlisted the developers at Big Boat Interactive, who include three developers from the 1998 Battlezone game and played a key part in keeping the community alive for 18 years.

We’re going to let Mike and the Big Boat guys loose on these community pages very soon, so watch out!

Rebellion’s first externally developed title
Hiring Big Boat Interactive to develop Battlezone 98 Redux marks another significant milestone for Rebellion too!

Since we self-published the PC editions of Sniper Elite V2 and Sniper Elite 3 games, Rebellion has changed from “just” being a games studio, to being one of the UK’s largest indie studio and publisher with the multi-format retail release of Zombie Army Trilogy in 2015 for PC, Xbox One and PlayStation 4.

Battlezone 98 Redux represents a new chapter in this journey, the first in a series of Rebellion IP to be developed out-of-house as our internal teams continue to crack on with Battlezone for PlayStation VR, and more unannounced “AAA” titles.

So for now, thank you for your support and we hope you’re as excited for Battlezone 98 Redux as we are!
http://i.imgur.com/9TZFYot.png
